detailed_source_records.title: Fix OpenAPI watch input classification and overlay hot reload
detailed_source_records.author: pmcelhaney
detailed_source_records.body:
## Summary

- add a shared `@counterfact/openapi` source classifier that recognizes parsed HTTP(S) URLs, converts `file:` URLs to local paths, preserves NUL rejection, and keeps ordinary names such as `httpspec.yaml` local
- make runtime and generator watchers observe every unique local OpenAPI input, including ordered overlays, while excluding remote inputs and the `_` sentinel
- reload the complete base-plus-overlay document when any local contributor changes, and document the resulting watch behavior
- extend the existing contract-evolution journey to prove that editing a local overlay updates the live server without a restart
- add patch changesets for `@counterfact/openapi`, `@counterfact/generator`, and `@counterfact/runtime`

## Verification

- focused OpenAPI, runtime, and generator tests: 4 suites, 26 tests passed
- full unit suite: 65 suites, 950 tests, and 127 snapshots passed
- build, typecheck, and lint passed
- focused contract-evolution black-box journey passed
- release preflight passed, including package boundaries, packaging dry runs, isolated package closures, and changeset validation

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] Start Counterfact with a local base document, a local overlay, `--watch`, and `--serve`; edit the overlay and confirm the affected endpoint changes without restarting the process.
- [x] Start Counterfact from a local file named `httpspec.yaml`; edit the file and confirm generated contracts and the running server reflect the change.
- [x] Use the `_` spec sentinel in a configuration that generates scenario/context artifacts and confirm Counterfact does not attempt to watch a file literally named `_`.

## Repository learning check

- Learning found: Yes
- Guidance updated: Yes
- Updated file(s): `.github/skills/counterfact-generator-internals/SKILL.md`
- Rationale: Generator watchers must classify sources through the shared OpenAPI contract, watch every unique local contributor, and regenerate from the complete ordered input set instead of inferring URL behavior from string prefixes.

detailed_source_records.title: fix(runtime): validate implicit 200 responses
detailed_source_records.author: pmcelhaney
detailed_source_records.body:
## Summary

- validate handler responses that omit `status` against the OpenAPI `200` response definition
- preserve explicit-status and `default` response behavior
- cover the regression through focused runtime tests and the shipped CLI journey
- document the implicit-success validation rule and release it with a runtime changeset

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

Fix the confirmed bug where response validation is bypassed when a handler relies on the implicit HTTP 200 status. Create a dedicated branch and PR with a changeset.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] A handler that omits `status` and a required `200` response header returns its body with a `response-type-error` header.
- [ ] Supplying the required header removes the validation error without requiring `status: 200`.
- [ ] A handler with an explicit non-200 status is validated against that response definition.
- [ ] An OpenAPI `default` response still applies when the effective status has no explicit response entry.

## Tasks

- Normalize response-spec selection to the effective HTTP status.
- Add unit, dispatcher, and black-box regression coverage.
- Update the response-validation FAQ and add a patch changeset.

## Verification

- `mise exec node@24 -- yarn build`
- `mise exec node@24 -- yarn workspace @counterfact/runtime test` — 28 suites, 367 tests passed
- `mise exec node@24 -- yarn typecheck`
- `mise exec node@24 -- yarn lint` — passed with existing warnings only
- `mise exec node@24 -- yarn test` — 64 suites, 945 tests, 127 snapshots passed
- Generated-OpenAPI black-box journey passed; the remaining four journeys also passed across the full/targeted runs
- `mise exec node@24 -- yarn test:packed-consumer`
- `mise exec node@24 -- yarn release:preflight`
- `git diff --check`

## Repository learning check

- Learning found: No
- Guidance updated: No
- Updated file(s): N/A
- Rationale: The defect is a localized status-default mismatch now captured by focused runtime and product-level regression tests; it did not reveal a new repository-wide contribution rule.

@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+---
+"@counterfact/runtime": patch
+---
+
+Validate responses that omit an explicit status against the OpenAPI `200` response definition.

@@ -203,7 +203,7 @@ Yes, for required query, header, and cookie parameters and supported JSON/form r
 
 ## Does it validate outgoing responses?
 
-Yes, by default. Response headers are validated against the schema defined in the spec. Any validation errors (missing required headers or type mismatches) are reported as `response-type-error` HTTP response headers — one header per error; multiple headers with the same name are allowed. The response body is still returned normally — the errors are advisory only. Disable this with `--no-validate-response` if you need looser behavior.
+Yes, by default. Response headers are validated against the schema defined in the spec. When a handler omits `status`, Counterfact validates it against the `200` response definition, matching the status sent over HTTP. Any validation errors (missing required headers or type mismatches) are reported as `response-type-error` HTTP response headers — one header per error; multiple headers with the same name are allowed. detailed_source_records.title: fix: harden OpenAPI routing and lifecycle cleanup
detailed_source_records.author: pmcelhaney
detailed_source_records.body:
## Summary

- prevent generated route paths and repository keys from escaping the output directory
- enforce URL segment boundaries and HTTP header case-insensitivity across routing, validation, coercion, and response generation
- safely encode client path parameters, inherit path-item parameters, and distinguish URLs from similarly named local files
- roll back partial startup and attempt every shutdown operation
- restore the no-emit typecheck, activate the missing-route regression test, and isolate REPL test streams

Each publishable behavior fix has its own patch changeset.

## Security impact

OpenAPI paths and repository keys now fail closed before any generated file operation if they are absolute, contain traversal or platform separators, or otherwise cannot be represented safely under the destination.

## Verification

- build, lint, typecheck, package boundaries, publishable-package checks
- 949 unit tests and 127 snapshots
- client, generator, runtime, REPL, OpenAPI, and Counterfact focused suites
- packed consumers and isolated package closures
- 5 black-box developer journeys
- type-definition tests and release preflight
- traced REPL suite with no MaxListeners warning

Native macOS watching hit the host file-descriptor ceiling during the combined suite; the complete suite passed with `CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING=1`, while package suites passed independently with native watching.

review_comments.author: Copilot
review_comments.body: OpenAPI operation parameters override path-item parameters by `(in, name)`, and header names are case-insensitive. With a path item declaring required `X-Token` and an operation overriding it with optional `x-token`, these keys remain distinct, so `missing()` still rejects a request that should be allowed and help lists both parameters. Normalize header names when forming the merge key.

review_comments.author: Copilot
review_comments.body: This `allSettled` call treats `moduleLoader.stopWatching()` as one shutdown operation, but that method closes its route watcher and scenario watcher sequentially. If the route watcher close rejects, the scenario watcher close is never attempted, so a watcher can still leak despite the new “attempt every” cleanup behavior. Make the module-loader cleanup all-settled as well (or expose/close both watchers independently).

review_comments.author: Copilot
review_comments.body: `normalizeOpenApiPath("")` returns `"/"` because of the `|| "/"` fallback, so `assertValidOpenApiPath` accepts an empty `paths` key as the root route. A spec containing `paths: { "": ... }` is therefore generated as `/index` instead of being rejected even though OpenAPI path keys must begin with `/`; preserve the root mapping only for an input of `/`, or reject the empty key before normalization.

review_comments.author: Copilot
review_comments.body: `resolveDestinationPath` runs inside each async mapper, so an unsafe entry later in `scripts` rejects only after earlier entries have already started reading contents and writing files. Direct mutation of the map can therefore leave partial output despite the new containment check. Preflight every repository key synchronously before constructing the write promises.

review_comments.author: Copilot
review_comments.body: The containment check is purely lexical (`resolve`/`relative`) and does not account for symlinks. If a pre-existing directory such as `destination/routes` points outside the destination, `routes/pets.ts` passes this check and `ensureDirectoryExists`/`writeFile` follows the link, writing generated content outside the output tree. Validate real path components or reject symlinked output components before writing.

review_comments.author: Copilot
review_comments.body: `escapePathForWindows()` is applied to the entire absolute candidate path, not just the repository-relative filename. On POSIX, a valid destination such as `/tmp/fixtures:1/output` is therefore rewritten to `/tmp/fixtures∶1/output`, so generated files are written outside the requested destination (or the write fails if that path does not exist). Preserve the resolved destination root and escape only the relative path segments, with platform-specific handling kept consistent with imports and pruning.

review_comments.author: Copilot
review_comments.body: This test stubs `repository.writeFiles`, so it only verifies that route/type writes were not reached. `CodeGenerator.generate()` initializes the cache directly before validating paths, meaning an invalid spec still creates `.gitignore` and `.cache/README.md` while this test passes. Assert those destination files are absent as well; the implementation must validate before cache initialization to satisfy the test name and fail-closed behavior.

review_comments.author: Copilot
review_comments.body: This parser now treats a local filename such as the added `httpspec.yaml` case as a filesystem path, but both `CodeGenerator.watch()` and `OpenApiDocument.watch()` still classify sources with `startsWith("http")`. Such a file is omitted from both watch lists (and with no overlays the generator watcher returns), so edits never regenerate output or reload the runtime document. Reuse the same URL classification in watcher setup.

detailed_source_records.title: fix(runtime): reload atomic store replacements
detailed_source_records.author: pmcelhaney
detailed_source_records.body:
## Summary

- make StoreLoader resilient to editor-style atomic replacements of `_.store.ts`
- coalesce shallow directory events, then reload only when the store source content changes
- preserve the live store object and last-good state across replacements and broken reloads
- supersedes #2292 with an implementation based on the monorepo runtime package

## Original Prompt

Make StoreLoader watch reliably on Windows and when editors save by replacing the store file.

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] Start a project with a stateful `_.store.ts`, mutate its live state, then save the file normally; confirm methods update without resetting state.
- [ ] Save `_.store.ts` using an editor that writes a temporary sibling and renames it over the original; confirm the store reloads without a transient deletion error.
- [ ] Change an unrelated file in the same directory; confirm no store reload occurs.
- [ ] Introduce a syntax error, then repair it; confirm the last good store remains active and the repaired source reloads.
- [ ] Repeat the replacement workflow on Windows; confirm watching remains reliable without forcing polling on other platforms.

## Tasks

- [x] Reconcile directory watcher events against the exact store source contents.
- [x] Serialize and flush debounced reconciliation during watcher shutdown.
- [x] Add regression coverage for temporary-file replacement and unrelated sibling changes.
- [x] Add a runtime patch changeset.

## Repository learning check

- [x] StoreLoader remains owned by `@counterfact/runtime`; no facade or REPL boundary changed.
- [x] The shared chokidar configuration still enables polling only on Windows.
- [x] Runtime lint, type build, focused StoreLoader tests, and the full runtime test directory pass.

## Verification

- `./node_modules/.bin/eslint packages/runtime/src/server/store-loader.ts packages/runtime/test/server/store-loader.test.ts`
- `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --build packages/types/tsconfig.json packages/openapi/tsconfig.json packages/runtime/tsconfig.json --force --pretty false`
- `CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING=true node --experimental-vm-modules ./node_modules/jest-cli/bin/jest.js --config jest.config.js packages/runtime/test/server/store-loader.test.ts --runInBand --forceExit --coverage=false`
- `CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING=true node --experimental-vm-modules ./node_modules/jest-cli/bin/jest.js --config jest.config.js packages/runtime/test --runInBand --forceExit --coverage=false`
- `git diff --check`

The polling override in the verification commands avoids the current macOS sandbox's file-descriptor limit; the production watcher configuration is unchanged and remains Windows-only.

detailed_source_records.title: Fix wide route random response typing
detailed_source_records.author: pmcelhaney
detailed_source_records.body:
## Summary

Make wide-route response helpers valid handler return values, including `.json()`, chained helpers, `.random()`, and `.stream()`.

## Root cause

`WideResponseBuilder` was not assignable to `COUNTERFACT_RESPONSE`, even though its fluent helpers return runtime response objects that a route handler can return directly. This caused valid wide-route implementations such as `$.x.response[200].json(...)` to fail type checking.

## Changes

- Make `WideResponseBuilder` a completed Counterfact response while preserving its fluent API.
- Ensure standard HTTP status codes such as `200` are available without an `undefined` result under strict indexed access.
- Type `.random()` as returning a fluent wide response.
- Type `.stream()` as a terminal response.
- Correct `.header()` to accept a header name and value.
- Add regression type tests for random, JSON, chained-header JSON, and stream responses.
- Add a patch changeset.

## Validation

- TypeScript compilation
- `tsd` type tests
- ESLint
- Unit tests: 873 passed
- Black-box tests: 13 passed

detailed_source_records.title: fix: add Koa Request type augmentation for body and rawBody
detailed_source_records.author: Copilot
detailed_source_records.body:
## Summary

`tsc --noEmit` was failing because `body` and `rawBody` don't exist on Koa's `Request` type. These properties are injected at runtime by `koa-bodyparser`, and `@types/koa-bodyparser` normally augments Koa's `Request` interface to match. However, `tsconfig.json` sets `"types": ["node"]` to prevent `@types/koa-bodyparser`'s bundled `@types/koa`/`@types/node` from conflicting with the project's own copies — which also suppresses the augmentation.

**Fix**: Added `src/server/web-server/koa-bodyparser.d.ts` — a local module augmentation that declares `body` and `rawBody` on Koa's `Request` interface, picked up automatically since `tsconfig.json` includes `src/`.

```ts
export {};

declare module "koa" {
  interface Request {
    body?: unknown;
    rawBody: string;
  }
}
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

Fix with Copilot: https://github.com/counterfact/api-simulator/actions/runs/30681583781/job/91319534656

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] Running `yarn tsc --noEmit` completes without errors
- [ ] Accessing `ctx.request.body` in `admin-api-middleware.ts` resolves without a TypeScript error
- [ ] Accessing `ctx.request.rawBody` in `routes-middleware.ts` resolves without a TypeScript error
- [ ] All existing tests pass (`yarn test`)

## Tasks

- Added `src/server/web-server/koa-bodyparser.d.ts` with a module augmentation for `koa` that adds `body?: unknown` and `rawBody: string` to `Request`

## Repository learning check

- Learning found: Yes
- Guidance updated: No
- Updated file(s): N/A
- Rationale: The pattern of using a local `.d.ts` module augmentation to expose runtime-injected properties when `tsconfig.json` restricts `types` is a useful repo-specific convention, but the existing skill files cover type augmentation patterns adequately and this is a narrow enough case that adding it would be noise rather than signal.

review_comments.body:
The middleware currently treats any `ctx.request.path` that `startsWith(prefix)` as eligible, which can incorrectly match unrelated paths (e.g. prefix "/api" also matches "/api2"). Also, when the request path equals the prefix exactly, `slice(prefix.length)` yields `""` rather than `"/"`, which then breaks proxy/method lookups for the OpenAPI root path.

This issue also appears on line 262 of the same file.

review_comments.author: Copilot
review_comments.body: `pruneTypes()` only preserves `types/versions.ts` when `this.version !== ""`. If a group mixes versioned and unversioned specs (allowed by validateSpecGroups via `group` vs `group@version` uniqueness), the unversioned runner will run `--prune --types` against the shared group directory and can delete `types/versions.ts` even though the group still has versioned specs and `types/versions.ts` is still required. The decision to keep `versions.ts` should be based on whether the *group* has any versions (e.g. `versions.length > 0` from ApiRunner/Dispatcher), not whether the current spec has a non-empty version.

+# Report 1: OpenAPI paths ending in `/` generate unusable dotfiles
+
+## Summary
+
+Counterfact generates malformed route and type filenames when an OpenAPI path ends with a trailing slash.
+
+For a path such as `/customers/`, generation produces files including:
+
+```text
+routes/customers/.ts
+types/paths/customers/.types.ts
+```
+
+The generated route is not registered for the intended `/customers/` URL, causing requests to return `404`.
+
+## Environment
+
+- Counterfact: `2.12.0`
+- Node.js: 24
+- OpenAPI: 3.0.3
+- Platform: macOS
+
+## Minimal reproduction
+
+```yaml
+openapi: 3.0.3
+
+info:
+  title: Trailing-slash reproduction
+  version: "1.0"
+
+paths:
+  /customers/:
+    get:
+      operationId: listCustomers
+      responses:
+        "200":
+          description: Success
+```
+
+Run:
+
+```sh
+npx counterfact openapi.yaml . --generate
+```
+
+## Actual behavior
+
+Counterfact generates:
+
+```text
+routes/customers/.ts
+types/paths/customers/.types.ts
+```
+
+The route module may subsequently be registered using its compiled filename rather than the intended collection path. A request to the declared path returns `404`:
+
+```sh
+curl -i http://localhost:3100/customers/
+```
+
+## Expected behavior
+
+A trailing slash in an OpenAPI path should normalize to a valid, visible route module:
+
+```text
+routes/customers.ts
+types/paths/customers.types.ts
+```
+
+The runtime should continue to accept both `/customers` and `/customers/`.
+
+## Impact
+
+Many APIs conventionally declare collection endpoints with trailing slashes. Such specifications cannot be generated reliably without modifying the contract first.
+
+The current behavior also creates hidden files that are easy to overlook in editors, file listings, and code review.
+
+## Current workaround
+
+Maintain two copies of the contract:
+
+1. An unchanged upstream copy.
+2. A runtime copy with trailing slashes removed from path keys.
+
+This works but creates contract duplication and requires a synchronization process.
+
+## Suggested resolution
+
+Normalize terminal slashes during path-to-filename conversion:
+
+- Map `/customers/` to the same generated filename as `/customers`.
+- Never generate an empty filename such as `.ts`.
+- Ensure the generated module registry maps the file back to the intended OpenAPI path.
+- Reject a document that declares both forms, such as `/customers` and `/customers/`, with a clear duplicate-normalized-path error.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- `/customers/` never generates `routes/customers/.ts`.
+- Generated route and type filenames are visible, valid filenames.
+- A request to `/customers/` reaches the generated handler.
+- Nested paths such as `/customers/{id}/` work.
+- Action paths such as `/subscriptions/{id}/cancel/` work.
+- Regeneration does not produce duplicate trailing and non-trailing route modules.
+- A document declaring both trailing and non-trailing forms fails generation clearly.
+- Tests cover root `/`, collection paths, parameterized paths, and nested action paths.

+# Report 2: Multiple API runners sharing a prefix do not fall through on unmatched routes
+
+## Summary
+
+Counterfact’s multi-spec mode cannot serve multiple OpenAPI documents at the same URL prefix.
+
+When multiple specifications use `prefix: ""`, every runner’s middleware matches every request. The first runner handles paths belonging to later runners and returns `404` instead of passing control to the next middleware.
+
+As a result, only the first API is reachable.
+
+## Environment
+
+- Counterfact: `2.12.0`
+- Node.js: 24
+- OpenAPI: 3.0.3
+- Platform: macOS
+
+## Configuration
+
+```yaml
+spec:
+  - source: ./customers.yml
+    group: customers
+    prefix: ""
+  - source: ./products.yml
+    group: products
+    prefix: ""
+
+destination: .
+```
+
+`customers.yml`:
+
+```yaml
+openapi: 3.0.3
+info:
+  title: Customers
+  version: "1.0"
+paths:
+  /customers:
+    get:
+      operationId: listCustomers
+      responses:
+        "200":
+          description: Success
+```
+
+`products.yml`:
+
+```yaml
+openapi: 3.0.3
+info:
+  title: Products
+  version: "1.0"
+paths:
+  /products:
+    get:
+      operationId: listProducts
+      responses:
+        "200":
+          description: Success
+```
+
+## Steps to reproduce
+
+Generate and serve the combined simulator:
+
+```sh
+npx counterfact --config counterfact.yaml --generate
+npx counterfact --config counterfact.yaml --serve
+```
+
+Request both APIs:
+
+```sh
+curl -i http://localhost:3100/customers
+curl -i http://localhost:3100/products
+```
+
+## Actual behavior
+
+The Customers runner is registered first and its middleware uses an empty prefix.
+
+Because every string starts with `""`, it claims `/products` even though the Customers registry has no matching route. The Customers dispatcher returns `404`, and the Products middleware never receives the request.
+
+## Expected behavior
+
+If a runner’s prefix matches but its route registry does not contain the requested path, Counterfact should call the next middleware.
+
+Expected routing:
+
+```text
+/customers
+  → Customers runner has route
+  → Customers handler
+
+/products
+  → Customers runner has no route
+  → fall through
+  → Products runner has route
+  → Products handler
+```
+
+## Impact
+
+Several OpenAPI documents describing subsets of one public API cannot be combined at their canonical paths.
+
+Users must instead assign artificial prefixes, which changes the simulated URLs and can duplicate resource names.
+
+For example:
+
+```text
+/customers/customers
+/products/products
+```
+
+This makes the simulator less representative of the real API.
+
+## Current workaround
+
+Allow Counterfact to derive distinct prefixes from group names:
+
+```yaml
+spec:
+  - source: ./customers.yml
+    group: customers
+  - source: ./products.yml
+    group: products
+```
+
+This avoids middleware collisions but changes the public paths.
+
+## Suggested resolution
+
+In multi-spec routing middleware:
+
+1. Check whether the request begins with the configured prefix.
+2. Strip the prefix.
+3. Check whether that runner’s registry contains a matching route or method.
+4. Call `next()` when no route exists.
+5. Dispatch only when the runner can handle the request.
+
+Care is needed for `405 Method Not Allowed`: Counterfact should return `405` only when the selected runner owns the path but not the method. It should continue searching other runners if another runner could own the same path and method.
+
+When multiple eligible runners define the same path and method, the first matching specification in configuration declaration order wins. If no runner supports the requested method but one or more own the path, return `405` with an `Allow` header that combines the methods from those runners.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- Two specifications can both use `prefix: ""`.
+- Routes unique to either specification remain reachable.
+- An unmatched route falls through to later runners.
+- `404` is returned only after all eligible runners decline the request.
+- `405` behavior remains correct.
+- Overlapping paths with different methods are handled deterministically.
+- Overlapping paths with the same method are handled by configuration declaration order.
+- Prefixes other than `""` retain their existing behavior.
+- Tests cover two and three runners sharing the same prefix.

+# Report 3: Multi-spec startup runs only the primary API’s scenario
+
+## Summary
+
+In multi-spec mode, Counterfact creates separate runners and scenario registries for every OpenAPI document, but server startup invokes the `startup` scenario only for the first runner.
+
+Startup scenarios belonging to subsequent API groups are never executed.
+
+## Environment
+
+- Counterfact: `2.12.0`
+- Node.js: 24
+- OpenAPI: 3.0.3
+- Platform: macOS
+
+## Example configuration
+
+```yaml
+spec:
+  - source: ./customers.yml
+    group: customers
+  - source: ./products.yml
+    group: products
+
+destination: .
+```
+
+Generated structure:
+
+```text
+customers/
+  routes/
+  scenarios/index.ts
+
+products/
+  routes/
+  scenarios/index.ts
+```
+
+Customers scenario:
+
+```ts
+export const startup: Scenario = ($) => {
+  $.context.seedCustomers([
+    {
+      id: "customer-001",
+      email: "ada@example.com",
+    },
+  ]);
+};
+```
+
+Products scenario:
+
+```ts
+export const startup: Scenario = ($) => {
+  $.context.seedProducts([
+    {
+      id: "product-001",
+      price: "19.99",
+    },
+  ]);
+};
+```
+
+## Actual behavior
+
+When the combined server starts:
+
+- The Customers `startup` scenario runs.
+- The Products `startup` scenario does not run.
+- Product routes begin with empty state.
+
+The application startup logic selects the first runner as `primaryRunner` and invokes its scenario registry only.
+
+## Expected behavior
+
+Every configured API group should have an opportunity to initialize its group state.
+
+A combined server startup should run:
+
+```text
+customers/scenarios/index.ts → startup
+products/scenarios/index.ts  → startup
+```
+
+Each scenario should receive the context registry for its group. All version runners within that group should share the same registry and therefore the same state. Separate groups retain separate context registries.
+
+When multiple versions share a group and therefore one physical scenario file, that group's startup scenario should run once.
+
+## Impact
+
+Multi-spec simulators cannot use Counterfact’s documented scenario convention consistently.
+
+This is especially problematic when:
+
+- Each API owns independent state.
+- The APIs are generated into separate groups.
+- Seeded data is required for useful startup behavior.
+- Related APIs need coherent fixtures.
+- Tests expect the combined server to be ready immediately after startup.
+
+Users must create custom bootstrap code, seed state directly in context constructors, or use private/internal runner objects.
+
+## Suggested resolution
+
+During server startup, invoke the startup scenario once for every configured group, in the group’s first declaration order, and pass each invocation that group’s shared context registry:
+
+```ts
+for (const group of groupsInDeclarationOrder) {
+  await runStartupScenario(
+    group.scenarioRegistry,
+    group.contextRegistry,
+    { port: config.port },
+    group.openApiDocument,
+  );
+}
+```
+
+If scenario order matters, execute them in specification declaration order instead of concurrently.
+
+An optional combined-server startup hook could also be useful for establishing cross-API relationships after individual groups initialize.
+
+## Design considerations
+
+- All version runners within a group must use the same context registry, not merely startup scenarios. Runners from different groups retain separate registries.
+- A failure must identify the group (and version, when relevant) whose startup failed and prevent the server from listening.
+- Startup order is configuration declaration order.
+- Multiple versioned specifications sharing a group must not initialize the shared state more than once.
+- Replacing the current runner-per-version architecture with one runner per group is future work and is not required to resolve this bug.
+- Existing single-spec behavior must remain unchanged.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- Every configured group’s `startup` scenario runs.
+- Every startup receives its group’s shared context.
+- State seeded for a group is visible to all versions of that group.
+- State remains isolated between different groups.
+- Declaration order is deterministic and documented.
+- A startup failure reports the relevant group.
+- Single-spec startup behavior remains compatible.
+- Versioned specs do not duplicate shared-state initialization.
+- Programmatic and CLI startup behave consistently.

+# Report 4: `--prune` leaves obsolete generated path-type dotfiles
+
+## Summary
+
+Counterfact’s `--prune` option does not consistently remove obsolete generated type files.
+
+After changing OpenAPI paths from trailing-slash forms to normalized forms and regenerating with `--prune`, obsolete route files were removed, but stale hidden type files remained under `types/paths/`.
+
+## Environment
+
+- Counterfact: `2.12.0`
+- Node.js: 24
+- OpenAPI: 3.0.3
+- Platform: macOS
+
+## Steps to reproduce
+
+Start with:
+
+```yaml
+paths:
+  /customers/:
+    get:
+      operationId: listCustomers
+      responses:
+        "200":
+          description: Success
+```
+
+Generate:
+
+```sh
+npx counterfact openapi.yaml . --generate
+```
+
+This creates files including:
+
+```text
+routes/customers/.ts
+types/paths/customers/.types.ts
+```
+
+Change the path:
+
+```yaml
+paths:
+  /customers:
+    get:
+      operationId: listCustomers
+      responses:
+        "200":
+          description: Success
+```
+
+Regenerate with pruning:
+
+```sh
+npx counterfact openapi.yaml . --generate --prune
+```
+
+## Actual behavior
+
+The normalized files are generated:
+
+```text
+routes/customers.ts
+types/paths/customers.types.ts
+```
+
+The obsolete hidden type file remains:
+
+```text
+types/paths/customers/.types.ts
+```
+
+In a six-spec package, this left 18 obsolete hidden type files after pruning.
+
+## Expected behavior
+
+`--prune` should remove every generator-owned artifact that no longer corresponds to the current OpenAPI document, including when generation is restricted to types.
+
+After pruning, only this file should remain:
+
+```text
+types/paths/customers.types.ts
+```
+
+## Impact
+
+Stale generated types:
+
+- Create confusing duplicate definitions.
+- Increase repository noise.
+- Can affect imports or editor indexing.
+- Are difficult to notice because their filenames begin with a dot.
+- Make `--prune` unreliable for contract updates.
+- Require manual deletion after regeneration.
+
+## Suggested resolution
+
+Extend pruning to build an expected-file set for every generator-owned artifact category:
+
+- Route modules
+- Path-operation types
+- Component types
+- Response types
+- Context-support types, where appropriate
+- Version metadata
+
+Then delete only generator-owned files absent from the expected set. Provenance should be established with Counterfact’s generated-file marker; user-authored route implementations must never be deleted.
+
+Generated files already contain a “do not edit” banner, which could help distinguish safe-to-prune output from user-authored files.
+
+## Safety considerations
+
+Pruning must never remove user-authored route implementations merely because a path disappears.
+
+If route and type pruning have different safety policies, Counterfact should expose separate options such as:
+
+```text
+--prune-routes
+--prune-types
+```
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- Obsolete `types/paths/**` files are removed by `--prune`.
+- Hidden files such as `.types.ts` are included.
+- All stale generator-owned artifact categories are pruned.
+- Type-only generation with `--prune` prunes stale generator-owned types.
+- Valid current path types are preserved.
+- User-authored files are protected according to documented pruning rules.
+- Pruning works in single-spec and multi-spec mode.
+- A second generation is idempotent.
+- Tests cover path renames, deletions, and trailing-slash normalization.

+# Report 5: Derived multi-spec group prefixes can duplicate existing resource paths
+
+## Summary
+
+Counterfact currently derives a URL prefix from each multi-spec `group` when `prefix` is omitted.
+
+When an OpenAPI document already includes the resource name in its paths, the resulting server URL duplicates that name.
+
+For example:
+
+```yaml
+group: customers
+```
+
+combined with:
+
+```yaml
+paths:
+  /customers:
+```
+
+produces:
+
+```text
+/customers/customers
+```
+
+This may be intentional behavior, but it is surprising and currently difficult to avoid because multiple runners cannot safely share `prefix: ""`.
+
+## Environment
+
+- Counterfact: `2.12.0`
+- Node.js: 24
+- OpenAPI: 3.0.3
+- Platform: macOS
+
+## Minimal configuration
+
+```yaml
+spec:
+  - source: ./customers.yml
+    group: customers
+  - source: ./products.yml
+    group: products
+
+destination: .
+```
+
+Customers specification:
+
+```yaml
+openapi: 3.0.3
+info:
+  title: Customers
+  version: "1.0"
+paths:
+  /customers:
+    get:
+      operationId: listCustomers
+      responses:
+        "200":
+          description: Success
+```
+
+## Actual behavior
+
+Counterfact derives `/customers` from the group and prepends it to the declared path.
+
+The effective endpoint becomes:
+
+```text
+/customers/customers
+```
+
+Likewise:
+
+```text
+/products/products
+/subscriptions/subscriptions
+/orders/orders
+```
+
+## Expected behavior
+
+Group names should organize generated files without changing URLs. In multi-spec mode, an omitted `prefix` should default to `""`, preserving paths exactly as declared by the OpenAPI document.
+
+Possible solutions include:
+
+### Selected behavior: group does not derive a URL prefix
+
+The following configuration should serve the declared `/customers` path at `/customers`, not `/customers/customers`:
+
+```yaml
+group: customers
+```
+
+## Impact
+
+The generated simulator no longer mirrors the API described by its OpenAPI documents.
+
+This affects:
+
+- Client configuration
+- Integration tests
+- Documentation examples
+- Drop-in replacement of real endpoints
+- Multi-spec APIs divided by domain
+- Developers diagnosing unexpected `404` responses
+
+## Documentation gap
+
+The configuration documentation should explain:
+
+- That `group` affects both generated directory layout and URL routing.
+- How a prefix is derived.
+- That the prefix is prepended to paths already present in the specification.
+- How to retain canonical paths.
+- Whether multiple specs may share a prefix.
+- How group names differ from URL prefixes.
+
+## Suggested resolution
+
+Remove automatic group-derived prefixes. An omitted `prefix` is the root prefix (`""`), and `group` affects generated directory layout only. Shared-prefix middleware fallthrough is required so root-mounted groups can coexist.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- Documentation shows the effective URL for grouped specifications.
+- Users can preserve paths exactly as declared across multiple specs.
+- Group names organize generated files without changing URLs.
+- Omitted `prefix` defaults to `""` in multi-spec mode.
+- Tests cover omitted, explicit, empty, and shared prefixes.

detailed_source_records.title: Watch code generation overlays for hot regeneration
detailed_source_records.author: Copilot
detailed_source_records.body:
## Summary

When an applied overlay file changes, generation now reruns the same way it does for OpenAPI source edits. This closes the gap where overlay-driven changes required manual regeneration.

- **Watch scope expanded**
  - `CodeGenerator.watch()` now watches all local generation inputs, not just the OpenAPI file:
    - local OpenAPI file + overlays for file-based specs
    - overlays only for HTTP OpenAPI sources
  - watch remains a no-op when there are no local watchable paths.

- **Overlay change regression coverage**
  - Added a focused server test that edits an applied overlay during watch mode and asserts regenerated type output changes accordingly.

```ts
const watchablePaths = this.openapiPath.startsWith("http")
  ? [...this.overlays]
  : [this.openapiPath, ...this.overlays];
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

<issue_title>Watch changes to overlay files</issue_title>
<issue_description>When an applied overlay file changes, the code should regenerate, just like when the OpenAPI document itself changes.</issue_description>

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] Run generator watch mode with a local OpenAPI file and one overlay, edit only the overlay, and observe regenerated output updates automatically.
- [ ] Run generator watch mode with an HTTP OpenAPI source plus a local overlay, edit only the overlay, and observe regeneration.
- [ ] Run generator watch mode with an HTTP OpenAPI source and no overlays, and observe that no local file watch behavior is started.
- [ ] Edit only the OpenAPI source (no overlay edits) and confirm existing regeneration behavior is unchanged.

## Tasks

- [x] Preserve existing no-op watch behavior when no local files are watchable.
- [x] Add targeted test coverage for regeneration triggered by overlay file edits.

detailed_source_records.title: fix: include path-item-level parameters in generated TypeScript types and server runtime
detailed_source_records.author: Copilot
detailed_source_records.body:
## Summary

OpenAPI allows parameters to be defined at the path item level (shared across all operations on that path), but both the TypeScript generator and the server dispatcher only read operation-level parameters — causing `path: never` in generated route handler types and missing type conversion (e.g. integer coercion) at runtime when parameters were declared at the path item level.

**Root cause (type generator):** `buildDollarArgType` called `this.requirement.get("parameters")` which only sees the operation object, never the parent path item.

**Root cause (server):** `operationForPathAndMethod` returned the raw operation object without merging path-item-level parameters, so `parameterTypes()`, `collectExplodedObjectParams()`, and `validateRequest()` all missed those parameters.

**Fix:** Both layers now merge path-item-level and operation-level parameters, with operation-level taking precedence on `name`+`in` collision per the OpenAPI specification. A new `parent` property on `Requirement` makes the path-item navigation direct and avoids URL string parsing. Merge logic in both layers uses a `Map` keyed on `"${in}:${name}"` for a clean O(n) implementation.

```yaml
# Before fix: generates `path: never` and skips integer coercion at runtime
paths:
  /stuff/{stuffId}:
    parameters:
      - name: stuffId
        in: path
        required: true
        schema:
          type: string
    get:
      responses:
        '204':
          description: successful
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

Parameters defined on the path level are ignored. The generated type in `types/paths/stuff/{stuffId}.types.ts` has `path: never` even though there should be the `stuffId` path parameter.

Parameters on path level are defined here: https://github.com/OAI/OpenAPI-Specification/blob/main/versions/3.1.2.md#fixed-fields-7

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] A spec with `parameters` defined only at the path item level generates a non-`never` `path` type in the corresponding `types/paths/…types.ts` file
- [x] A spec with parameters at both path item level and operation level produces merged types, with the operation-level entry overriding the path-level one when they share the same `name` and `in`
- [x] A spec with parameters only at the operation level continues to generate correct types (no regression)
- [x] At runtime, an integer parameter defined at the path item level is correctly coerced from a URL string to a number before being passed to the handler
- [x] Required parameters defined at the path item level are validated on incoming requests (missing parameter returns 400)

## Tasks

detailed_source_records.title: fix: cast OAS3 schema-typed parameters at runtime
detailed_source_records.author: Copilot
detailed_source_records.body:
## Summary

OAS3 places parameter types under `parameter.schema.type` rather than the OAS2 top-level `parameter.type`. The dispatcher's `parameterTypes()` only read the OAS2 field, so path/query/header parameters declared OAS3-style were never cast — e.g. `$.path.petId` remained `"1"` (string) instead of `1` (number).

**Fix:** one-line fallback in `Dispatcher.parameterTypes()`:

```ts
// Before
const type = parameter?.type;

// After
const type = parameter?.type ?? parameter?.schema?.type;
```

**Test:** new dispatcher test mirrors the existing OAS2 casting test but uses `schema: { type: "integer" }` etc. to cover the OAS3 path end-to-end.

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

When a parameter is not a string per the OpenAPI spec the server should perform type conversions as necessary.

For example when GET /pet/1 is called, $.path.petId should be a number not a string.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] `GET /pet/1` where `petId` is declared as OAS3 `schema: { type: "integer" }` — `$.path.petId` is the number `1`, not the string `"1"`
- [ ] `GET /pets?limit=10` where `limit` is declared as OAS3 `schema: { type: "integer" }` — `$.query.limit` is the number `10`, not `"10"`
- [ ] A header declared `schema: { type: "boolean" }` with raw value `"true"` arrives as the boolean `true` in the handler
- [ ] OAS2-style `type: "integer"` path/query/header parameters still cast correctly (regression)
- [ ] String parameters remain strings under both OAS2 and OAS3 declaration styles

## Tasks

- Fixed `Dispatcher.parameterTypes()` in `src/server/dispatcher.ts` to fall back to `parameter.schema?.type` when `parameter.type` is absent
- Added a new test in `test/server/dispatcher.test.ts` covering OAS3 schema-typed path, query, and header parameter casting
- Added a patch changeset

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+---
+"counterfact": patch
+---
+
+Cast parameters at runtime: parameters defined with OAS3-style schema types (e.g. `schema: { type: "integer" }`) are now correctly cast to their declared JavaScript types in route handlers. For example, when `GET /pet/1` is called, `$.path.petId` will be a number rather than a string when the OpenAPI spec declares it as `integer`.

detailed_source_records.title: Fix: Query params of type object are now exploded correctly (OpenAPI default)
detailed_source_records.author: Copilot
detailed_source_records.body:
## Summary

OpenAPI 3.x defaults query parameters of type `object` to `style: form, explode: true`, which means each property is sent as its own query param (e.g. `?page=0&size=100&sort=name`). Counterfact was looking for the literal parameter name (`pageable`) in the query string, producing a false 400 "required" error and never assembling the object for the handler.

**Validation** (`src/server/request-validator.ts`)
- Added `isExplodedObjectQueryParam()` — detects object-type query params using the OpenAPI 3.x default serialisation rules (`style: form`, `explode: true`)
- `findMissingRequired()` now considers a required object param satisfied when any of its schema-declared properties appear in the query string

**Object reconstruction** (`src/server/dispatcher.ts`)
- Added `collectExplodedObjectParams()` — gathers flat query keys that match a parameter's schema properties back under the parameter name before the handler is called
- Handler receives `$.query.pageable = { page: "0", size: "100" }` instead of bare `$.query.page` etc.
- Unrelated query params remain at the top level of `$.query`

**Type updates** (`src/counterfact-types/open-api-parameters.ts`)
- Added `style?: string`, `explode?: boolean`, and `properties` to `OpenApiParameters` so the checks are type-safe

Setting `explode: false` on a parameter in the spec opts out of this behaviour and restores the previous lookup-by-name semantics.

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

**Bug: Query Params of Type Object do not explode**

When a query parameter is declared with a schema of `type: object` (e.g. `Pageable` with `page`, `size`, `sort`), calling the endpoint with exploded properties (`?page=0&size=100&sort=a`) returns:

> Request validation failed: query parameter 'pageable' is required

According to the OpenAPI spec, `in: query` parameters default to `style: form, explode: true`, so each object property should map to its own query param. The validator incorrectly expects a literal `pageable` key. Setting `style: form, explode: true` explicitly has no effect.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] `GET /test?page=0&size=100` no longer returns 400 when `pageable` is a required object-type query parameter
- [x] The handler receives `$.query.pageable` as a reconstructed object (`{ page: "0", size: "100" }`) rather than having those keys only at the top level
- [x] Sending no `pageable` properties when the parameter is `required: true` still returns 400 mentioning the parameter name
- [x] A query parameter with `explode: false` in the spec is still resolved by its own name (no regression)
- [x] Unrelated query params not in the object schema remain accessible directly on `$.query`

## Tasks

- Added `isExplodedObjectQueryParam()` to `request-validator.ts` (exported) and wired it into `findMissingRequired()`
- Added `collectExplodedObjectParams()` to `dispatcher.ts`; applied it between validation and handler dispatch
- Broadened `DispatcherRequest.query` to `string | string[]` to match Koa's actual parsed type
- Updated `OpenApiParameters` with `style`, `explode`, and `schema.properties`
- Added 4 new tests covering acceptance, rejection, reconstruction, and preservation of unrelated params
- Added patch changeset and documented exploded object query params in `docs/features/routes.md`

+---
+"counterfact": patch
+---
+
+Fix: query parameters of type object with exploded form style (the OpenAPI default) are now properly supported. The request validator no longer falsely reports required object parameters as missing when their properties are sent as individual query params (e.g. `?page=0&size=100`). The handler receives the object assembled under the parameter name (`$.query.pageable`) rather than only the flat individual keys.

+### Object query parameters (exploded form style)
+
+When a query parameter has `type: object` in the spec, OpenAPI's default serialisation is _exploded form style_: each property of the object becomes its own query parameter.
+
+For example, a `pageable` parameter of type `Pageable` (with `page`, `size`, and `sort` properties) is sent like this:
+
+```
+GET /items?page=0&size=100&sort=name
+```

+Counterfact automatically assembles these individual query parameters back into the object, so you can access them as:

+  // ...
+};
+```

+This behaviour follows the OpenAPI 3.x defaults (`style: form`, `explode: true`) and also applies when those values are set explicitly. To opt out, set `explode: false` on the parameter in your spec.
+
 ## Basic auth: `$.auth`
 
 When a request includes HTTP Basic credentials, they're available at `$.auth.username` and `$.auth.password`.

detailed_source_records.title: Handle `_.context` syntax/import failures without crashing startup
detailed_source_records.author: Copilot
detailed_source_records.body:
## Summary

A broken `_.context.ts` (syntax/import error) previously bubbled into startup failure paths. This change makes context-module load failures non-fatal: Counterfact now warns and skips that context module, while continuing to load routes.

- **Context load error handling**
  - In `ModuleLoader.loadEndpoint`, context files (`_.context.*`) now take a dedicated error path on import failure.
  - Instead of registering route-style 500 handlers or throwing, loader writes a warning and returns.
- **Route error behavior unchanged**
  - Non-context route modules still keep existing behavior (500 responder registration for import/syntax failures).
- **Docs update**
  - Added explicit note in state docs that invalid `_.context.ts` is skipped with a warning.
- **Release metadata**
  - Added a patch changeset describing the behavior change.

```ts
if (this.isContextFile(pathName)) {
  const warning = isSyntaxError
    ? `Warning: There is a syntax error in the context file: ${displayPath}`
    : `Warning: There was an error loading the context file: ${displayPath}`;

  process.stdout.write(`\n${warning}\n`);
  return;
}
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

**Issue title:** App should not crash due to syntax error in _.context.ts

**Issue description:** A syntax error in _.context.ts should not cause the app to crash. Instead it should print a warning and not load the context module.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] Start Counterfact with a project whose `routes/_.context.ts` contains invalid syntax; verify startup continues and a warning is printed mentioning the context file.
- [ ] With the same invalid `_.context.ts`, call a normal route module in that tree and verify it still responds (app remains operational).
- [ ] Confirm the broken context is not applied (state/methods from that context are unavailable) until the file is fixed.
- [ ] Introduce a syntax error in a route file (not `_.context.ts`) and verify existing route-error behavior is unchanged (generated 500 response path still applies).

## Tasks

- Added context-specific import-error handling in `src/server/module-loader.ts` to warn + skip for `_.context.*`.
- Added focused regression test in `test/server/module-loader.test.ts` for invalid `_.context.js` behavior (warning emitted, route still loaded, context not registered).
- Updated docs in `docs/features/state.md` to document warning-and-skip behavior for invalid context files.
- Added patch changeset in `.changeset/free-numbers-relate.md`.

+---
+"counterfact": patch
+---
+
+Warn and skip loading context modules when they fail to import, including syntax errors in \_.context files.

detailed_source_records.title: Add runtime response header validation with OpenAPI hot-reload
detailed_source_records.author: Copilot
detailed_source_records.body:
## Summary

Validates response headers at runtime against the OpenAPI spec and reports errors as `response-type-error` HTTP headers — one header per error, with the same name repeated for multiple errors. Enabled by default; disable with `--no-validate-response`. Changes to the OpenAPI spec file are picked up automatically without a server restart.

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] Start counterfact against a spec with a required response header; call the route without setting it — verify a `response-type-error` header describes the missing header
- [ ] Return a response header with the wrong type (e.g. `"not-a-number"` for an `integer` header) — verify a `response-type-error` header appears with a descriptive message
- [ ] Return multiple invalid headers — verify multiple `response-type-error` headers appear (one per error, same header name)
- [ ] Return all required response headers with correct types — verify no `response-type-error` headers appear
- [ ] Start counterfact with `--no-validate-response` — verify no `response-type-error` headers appear even when headers are invalid
- [ ] Routes with no response header schemas in the spec behave unchanged (no error headers added)
- [ ] Edit the local OpenAPI spec file while the server is running — verify subsequent requests use the updated validation rules without restarting

## Tasks

- **`src/server/response-validator.ts`** (new) — AJV-based validator: checks required headers are present and header values match their schema types; coerces integer/number/boolean strings before validation; falls back to `default` response spec when the specific status code isn't defined
- **`src/server/registry.ts`** — Added `appendedHeaders?: [string, string][]` to `CounterfactResponseObject` to explicitly represent repeated same-name headers as individual entries
- **`src/server/dispatcher.ts`** — After normalizing the response, runs `validateResponse` when `config.validateResponses !== false`; maps each error to a separate `["response-type-error", error]` tuple in `appendedHeaders` — one entry per error, no array bundling under a single key
- **`src/server/koa-middleware.ts`** — Iterates `response.appendedHeaders` and calls `ctx.res.appendHeader` once per entry, sending each as a genuinely separate HTTP header
- **`src/server/config.ts`** — Added `validateResponses: boolean`
- **`bin/counterfact.js`** — Added `--no-validate-response` flag; wired to `validateResponses` in the config object
- **`src/server/load-openapi-document.ts`** (new) — Extracted `loadOpenApiDocument` from `app.ts` into its own server-side module; re-exported from `app.ts` for backward compatibility
- **`src/server/openapi-watcher.ts`** (new) — `OpenApiWatcher` class with `watch()` / `stopWatching()` methods; watches a local OpenAPI spec file with chokidar and updates `dispatcher.openApiDocument` on every `change` event so validation reflects the latest spec without a restart; skips URL-based specs
- **`src/app.ts`** — Instantiates `OpenApiWatcher` and calls `watch()` / `stopWatching()` alongside the other watchers; no longer contains any inline file-watching logic
- **Tests** — `test/server/response-validator.test.ts` (15 cases); dispatcher tests updated to assert on `appendedHeaders` for required-header missing, wrong type, valid, and disabled scenarios
- **Docs** — `docs/reference.md` and `docs/faq.md` updated to document the feature and the new flag

detailed_source_records.title: fix: escape XML special characters in jsonToXml text content
detailed_source_records.author: Bahtya
detailed_source_records.body:
## Problem

In `src/server/json-to-xml.ts`, the `jsonToXml` function escapes attribute values via `xmlEscape()` but does **not** escape text content in the fallback branch for primitive values:

```ts
return `<${name}>${String(json)}</${name}>`;
```

If the string contains `<`, `>`, `&`, `"` or ``, the output will be malformed XML. For example, `jsonToXml("<script>alert(1)</script>", undefined, "data")` produces `<data><script>alert(1)</script></data>` — broken XML.

## Fix

Apply the existing `xmlEscape()` function to `String(json)` in the text content branch:

```ts
return `<${name}>${xmlEscape(String(json))}</${name}>`;
```

## Testing

Added two new test cases:
- Escaping `<script>alert("xss")</script>` in text content
- Escaping `&`, `<`, `>` in a mixed string

Fixes #1739

detailed_source_records.title: Fix Tools.accepts() failing when Accept header has spaces after commas
detailed_source_records.author: Copilot
detailed_source_records.body:
`Tools.accepts()` incorrectly returned `false` for valid Accept headers like `"text/html, application/json"` because tokens weren't trimmed after splitting on `","`, leaving a leading space that broke the type comparison.

## Summary

Single-char fix: `.trim()` each token before splitting on `"/"`.

```ts
// Before
const [type, subtype] = acceptType.split("/");
// After
const [type, subtype] = acceptType.trim().split("/");
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

`Tools.accepts()` splits on `","` but does not trim whitespace from each part. This produces `[" application/json"]` (with a leading space) as the second element. When that is further split on `"/"`, the type becomes `" application"` rather than `"application"`, so the comparison always fails and `accepts()` returns `false` even when the type is listed in the Accept header.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] `Tools.accepts('application/json')` returns `true` when Accept header is `"text/html, application/json"` (space after comma)
- [ ] `Tools.accepts('text/html')` returns `true` when Accept header is `"text/html"` (no change to single-type behavior)
- [ ] `Tools.accepts('text/html')` returns `true` when Accept header is `"text/*"` (wildcard subtype still works)
- [ ] `Tools.accepts('application/json')` returns `false` when Accept header is `"text/*"` (rejection still works)
- [ ] `Tools.accepts('what/ever')` returns `true` when Accept header is `undefined` (missing header still accepts all)

## Tasks

- Added `.trim()` to each `acceptType` token before splitting on `"/"` in `src/server/tools.ts`
- Added test case for space-separated Accept header to the `it.each` truth table in `test/server/tools.test.ts`

detailed_source_records.title: fix: Tools.accepts() case-insensitive accept header lookup
detailed_source_records.author: Copilot
detailed_source_records.body:
`Tools.accepts()` read `this.headers.Accept` (capital A), but Node.js normalizes all incoming HTTP header names to lowercase. In production, `this.headers.Accept` is always `undefined`, triggering the early-return guard and making `accepts()` unconditionally return `true`.

## Summary

Replace the direct key lookup with a case-insensitive search so `accept`, `Accept`, and `ACCEPT` all resolve correctly.

```ts
// Before — broken in production (Node.js lowercases all headers)
const acceptHeader = this.headers.Accept;

// After — handles any casing
const acceptHeader = Object.entries(this.headers).find(
  ([key]) => key.toLowerCase() === "accept",
)?.[1];
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

`Tools.accepts()` reads `this.headers.Accept` (capital A). Node.js normalises all incoming HTTP header names to **lowercase**, so when a real HTTP request is processed via Koa the header is stored under `accept` (lowercase). `this.headers.Accept` is therefore always `undefined` in production.

Because `undefined` triggers the early-return guard `if (acceptHeader === "" || acceptHeader === undefined) { return true; }`, the method unconditionally returns `true` — completely ignoring the client's actual Accept header.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] `Tools.accepts("application/json")` returns `false` when the request carries a lowercase `accept: text/plain` header
- [ ] `Tools.accepts("text/html")` returns `true` when the request carries `accept: text/html`
- [ ] `Tools.accepts("text/html")` returns `true` when the request carries `Accept: text/html` (capital A, e.g. from a browser or curl)
- [ ] `Tools.accepts("application/json")` returns `true` when no `accept` header is present (existing permissive behavior unchanged)
- [ ] A route handler that gates response type on `tools.accepts()` returns `406 Not Acceptable` when the client sends an incompatible `accept` header in a real Koa request

## Tasks

- Added failing test: `accepts('application/json') returns false when lowercase 'accept' header is 'text/plain'`
- Replaced `this.headers.Accept` with a case-insensitive `Object.entries()` lookup in `src/server/tools.ts`

detailed_source_records.title: Fix: Dispatcher proxy() always throws when request body is present
detailed_source_records.author: Copilot
detailed_source_records.body:
`proxy()` in the Dispatcher was broken in two ways: `headers.contentType` (camelCase) was used instead of `headers["content-type"]` (kebab-case), causing the guard to always evaluate as `true`; and the guard itself unnecessarily restricted proxying to `application/json` requests only.

## Summary

Remove the content-type restriction from `proxy()` entirely so it works for all content types. Rather than re-serializing the parsed body, `proxy()` now forwards `ctx.request.rawBody` — the original wire bytes stored by `koa-bodyparser` before parsing — directly to `fetch()`. This eliminates all re-serialization and correctly handles every content type, including those with charset suffixes (e.g. `application/json; charset=utf-8`).

```ts
// Before (broken — threw for every request with a body)
if (body !== undefined && headers.contentType !== "application/json") {
  throw new Error(`$.proxy() is currently limited to application/json requests...`);
}
body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),

// After — no restriction, no re-serialization; raw wire bytes forwarded as-is
body: body === undefined ? undefined : rawBody,
```

`koa-bodyparser` unconditionally sets `returnRawBody: true` on `co-body` internally, so `ctx.request.rawBody` is always available as the unparsed string for any request that has a body.

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

`proxy()` in the Dispatcher had a guard that threw when the request body was present and the content-type was not `application/json`. The guard used `headers.contentType` (camelCase) instead of `headers["content-type"]` (kebab-case), so it was always `undefined`, making the condition always `true` — causing `proxy()` to throw for every request carrying a body, including valid `application/json` POSTs.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] `POST /any-route` with `content-type: application/json` and a JSON body successfully proxies through without throwing
- [ ] `POST /any-route` with `content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8` and a JSON body successfully proxies through (charset suffix handled correctly)
- [ ] `POST /any-route` with `content-type: text/plain` and a plain-text body successfully proxies through without throwing
- [ ] `POST /any-route` with `content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and a body successfully proxies through without throwing
- [ ] `GET /any-route` with no body proxies normally (unchanged behavior)
- [ ] The upstream response body and headers are returned correctly regardless of content type

## Tasks

- Remove the content-type restriction guard from `proxy()` in `src/server/dispatcher.ts`
- Add `rawBody?: string` to `DispatcherRequest` type
- In `koa-middleware.ts`, declare `rawBody` on the Koa `Request` interface, destructure `ctx.request.rawBody`, and pass it through to `dispatcher.request()` (excluded for GET/HEAD, consistent with `body`)
- In `dispatcher.ts`, destructure `rawBody` in `request()` and use `body === undefined ? undefined : rawBody` in `proxy()` — no re-serialization of any kind
- Update tests: pass `rawBody` alongside `body` and verify the exact string forwarded to upstream `fetch` is the raw wire bytes unchanged

issue_comments.author: Copilot
issue_comments.body:
> Remove the limitation so the proxy works for all content types. 

Done in 9b5c46c. Removed the content-type guard entirely. The proxy now forwards all content types. Body serialization uses `JSON.stringify` only for `application/json`; all other content types pass the body through as `String(body)` (which is correct for the `text/*` and similar cases that Koa's body parser produces).

issue_comments.author: Copilot
issue_comments.body:
> Why does it need to serialize the body? Did Koa parse it? 
> 
> What is the content-type has an encoding attached?...

Good questions — addressed in the latest commit.

1. **Yes, Koa already parses it.** `ctx.request.body` is deserialized by Koa's body parser before it reaches the dispatcher: `application/json` → JavaScript object, `text/*` → string. So the proxy does need to re-serialize the object back to a string before handing it to `fetch`.

2. **Charset suffix.** `"application/json; charset=utf-8" === "application/json"` is `false`, so the old content-type string check was fragile. The new check avoids the header entirely.

3. **`typeof body === "object"`** is the right discriminator here: if Koa gave us a parsed object, stringify it; if it gave us a string, pass it through. Done in the latest commit.

issue_comments.author: Copilot
issue_comments.body:
> Is there a way to get the raw request body before body-parser 

Yes — `koa-bodyparser` unconditionally sets `returnRawBody: true` on `co-body` internally, so `ctx.request.rawBody` always holds the original wire bytes as a string. Updated in the latest commit to thread `rawBody` from the Koa context all the way through to `proxy()`, so `fetch` receives the unparsed body directly with no re-serialization at all.

detailed_source_records.title: Improve error messages for malformed OpenAPI specs
detailed_source_records.author: Copilot
detailed_source_records.body:
## Summary

A bad or partial OpenAPI document produced a raw JavaScript stack trace instead of a user-facing message. This replaces those stack traces with clear, actionable errors that include the spec path and the underlying cause.

**Before:**
```
ResolverError: Error opening file /path/to/bad-spec.yaml: ENOENT: no such file or directory
    at Object.read (node_modules/@apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser/dist/lib/resolvers/file.js:74:19)
    at ...
```

**After:**
```
❌ Could not load the OpenAPI spec from "bad-spec.yaml".
Error opening file /path/to/bad-spec.yaml: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/path/to/bad-spec.yaml'
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

A bad or partial OpenAPI document currently produces a JavaScript stack trace, not a user-facing message pointing at the problem. Given that users feed arbitrary specs to this tool, clear, actionable errors at this boundary would meaningfully reduce friction.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] Running `counterfact nonexistent.yaml ./api` prints a `❌` message containing the spec path and a clear reason (e.g. ENOENT), with no stack trace
- [x] Running with a spec that has a broken `$ref` (pointing to a missing file) prints a user-friendly error, not a raw exception
- [x] Running `counterfact _ ./api` (no-spec mode) starts normally without any spec-loading error
- [x] Running with a valid spec still works as before — routes and types are generated correctly
- [x] A spec that fails to load during `--generate` prints only the friendly error message and exits cleanly

## Tasks

- **`specification.ts`** — `load()` wraps `bundle()` errors: catches, formats a `Could not load the OpenAPI spec from "..."` message, re-throws with `{ cause }` preserved
- **`app.ts`** — `loadOpenApiDocument()` throws the same friendly error format instead of silently returning `undefined`; `counterfact()` and `start()` skip spec loading and code generation/watching when `openApiPath === "_"` (run-without-spec mode); removed now-dead `undefined` guard in `createMswHandlers()`
- **`bin/counterfact.js`** — wrapped both `await counterfact(config)` and `await start(config)` in `try/catch`; on failure, prints only `error.message` prefixed with `❌` and exits cleanly — no stack trace exposed to the user
- **`test/app.test.ts`** — changed mock config `openApiPath` from the non-existent `"foo.yaml"` to `"_"` so tests no longer rely on silent spec-load failure
- **`specification.test.ts`** — added three error-handling tests: file not found, broken `$ref`, and verifying ENOENT details appear in the thrown message

@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+---
+title: "Bug: Dispatcher proxy() always throws when request body is present"
+parentIssue: 1650
+labels:
+  - bug
+assignees: []
+milestone:
+---
+
+The `proxy()` helper inside `Dispatcher.request()` is meant to reject non-JSON requests with a helpful error. The guard is:
+
+```ts
+if (body !== undefined && headers.contentType !== "application/json") {
+  throw new Error(...);
+}
+```
+
+The problem is `headers.contentType` (camelCase). HTTP headers use kebab-case (`content-type`), and the `headers` object never has a `contentType` key. `headers.contentType` is always `undefined`, so `undefined !== "application/json"` is always `true`.
+
+The entire condition reduces to `body !== undefined`, meaning the proxy throws for **every** request that carries a body — including valid `application/json` POST requests.
+
+## Failing test
+
+Added in `test/server/dispatcher.proxy.test.ts`:
+
+```
+does not throw when proxying a POST request with a JSON body and content-type: application/json
+```
+
+Run `yarn test` and look for that test name in the `a dispatcher passes a proxy function to the operation` describe block.
+
+## Root cause
+
+```ts
+// src/server/dispatcher.ts
+if (body !== undefined && headers.contentType !== "application/json") {
+  //                             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ should be headers["content-type"]
+```
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- [ ] `headers.contentType` is replaced with `headers["content-type"]`
+- [ ] The previously failing test passes
+- [ ] The existing proxy test continues to pass
+- [ ] A POST request with a non-JSON content type is still rejected with the descriptive error

@@ -0,0 +1,35 @@
+---
+title: "Bug: Tools.accepts() ignores lowercase 'accept' header — always returns true in production"
+parentIssue: 1650
+labels:
+  - bug
+assignees: []
+milestone:
+---
+
+`Tools.accepts()` reads `this.headers.Accept` (capital A). Node.js normalises all incoming HTTP header names to **lowercase**, so when a real HTTP request is processed via Koa the header is stored under `accept` (lowercase). `this.headers.Accept` is therefore always `undefined` in production.
+
+Because `undefined` triggers the early-return guard `if (acceptHeader === "" || acceptHeader === undefined) { return true; }`, the method unconditionally returns `true` — completely ignoring the client's actual Accept header.
+
+## Failing test
+
+Added in `test/server/tools.test.ts`:
+
+```
+accepts('application/json') returns false when lowercase 'accept' header is 'text/plain'
+```
+
+Run `yarn test` and look for that test name in the `tools` describe block.
+
+## Root cause
+
+```ts
+// src/server/tools.ts
+const acceptHeader = this.headers.Accept; // ← should be this.headers.accept
+```
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- [ ] `this.headers.Accept` is replaced by a case-insensitive lookup (or lowercased key lookup) so that `accept`, `Accept`, and `ACCEPT` all work
+- [ ] The previously failing test passes
+- [ ] All other `accepts()` tests continue to pass

@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+---
+title: "Bug: Tools.accepts() fails when Accept header has spaces after commas"
+parentIssue: 1650
+labels:
+  - bug
+assignees: []
+milestone:
+---
+
+A well-formed HTTP Accept header commonly separates values with `", "` (comma followed by a space), e.g. `"text/html, application/json"`.
+
+`Tools.accepts()` splits on `","` but does **not** trim whitespace from each part. This produces `[" application/json"]` (with a leading space) as the second element. When that is further split on `"/"`, the type becomes `" application"` rather than `"application"`, so the comparison against the requested content type always fails and `accepts()` returns `false` even when the type is listed in the Accept header.
+
+## Failing test
+
+Added in `test/server/tools.test.ts`:
+
+```
+accepts('application/json') returns true when Accept header is 'text/html, application/json' (with space)
+```
+
+Run `yarn test` and look for that test name in the `tools` describe block.
+
+## Root cause
+
+```ts
+// src/server/tools.ts
+const acceptTypes = String(acceptHeader).split(",");
+return acceptTypes.some((acceptType) => {
+  const [type, subtype] = acceptType.split("/"); // " application" has a leading space
+  ...
+});
+```
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- [ ] Each token is trimmed (e.g. `acceptType.trim()`) before being split on `"/"`
+- [ ] The previously failing test passes
+- [ ] All other `accepts()` tests continue to pass

detailed_source_records.title: Fix: syntax error in a route file no longer crashes the server
detailed_source_records.author: Copilot
detailed_source_records.body:
A syntax error in a CommonJS route file would crash Counterfact via an unhandled promise rejection. `require()` throws synchronously on parse failure; the existing `.catch()` only handled promise rejections, so the error re-threw past `void loadEndpoint(...)`.

## Summary

**Root cause:** `uncached-require.cjs` called `require()` synchronously inside `Promise.resolve(...)`, so a `SyntaxError` escaped before `.catch()` could intercept it. The outer `catch` re-threw, producing an unhandled rejection.

**Fix:**
- **`uncached-require.cjs`** — wrap `require()` in `try/catch`, return `Promise.reject(error)` on failure so errors are always promise rejections
- **`module-loader.ts` (`loadEndpoint`)** — capture import errors and register a stub `Module` for all HTTP methods that returns `500` with an informative message:
  - `SyntaxError` → `"There is a syntax error in the route file: <path>"`
  - Other errors → `"There was an error loading the route file: <path>"`
- When the file is fixed and the watcher fires again, `registry.add` overwrites the stub with the real handler

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

If a file under `./routes` has a syntax error, Counterfact currently crashes.

The server should not crash. Requests to that route should return a 500 error with a message: "There is a syntax error in the route file: ./routes/my/path.ts"

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] Saving a route file with a syntax error (e.g. `const = 1;`) does not crash the server
- [x] A `GET` request to a route whose file has a syntax error returns HTTP 500 with a message containing "syntax error" and the file path
- [x] All other routes continue to respond normally while one route file is broken
- [x] Fixing the syntax error and saving the file causes the route to respond correctly (stub is replaced by real handler)
- [x] A `.cjs` CommonJS route file with a syntax error also returns 500 instead of crashing (this was the primary crash path)
- [x] Deleting a broken route file removes the 500 stub from the registry

## Tasks

- Wrap `require()` in `try/catch` in `uncached-require.cjs` to convert synchronous throws into `Promise.reject`
- Capture import errors in `loadEndpoint` and register a 500 stub module covering all HTTP methods
- Add tests for ESM and CJS route files with syntax errors
- Add changeset entry

detailed_source_records.title: Fix reserved keyword operationId causing TypeScript syntax errors
detailed_source_records.author: Copilot
detailed_source_records.body:
## Summary

When an OpenAPI spec uses a JS/TS reserved keyword (e.g. `delete`, `import`, `type`) as an `operationId`, Counterfact emits invalid TypeScript like `import type { delete } from ...`, crashing with a `SyntaxError`. The fix appends `_` to any sanitized identifier that collides with a reserved word.

```ts
// operationId "delete" → "delete_"
export type delete_ = { ... };
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

OpenAPI specs that use reserved words as `operationId` (valid per the spec, accepted by Swagger Editor) caused a `SyntaxError` in generated TypeScript. Example: `operationId: delete` produced `import type { delete } from ...`.

Maintainer direction: append `_` to the identifier and leave an explanatory comment.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] An OpenAPI spec with `operationId: delete` generates valid TypeScript (no `SyntaxError` on import)
- [ ] The generated type name is `delete_` (not `delete`)
- [ ] Other reserved words (`import`, `type`, `return`, etc.) are similarly suffixed with `_`
- [ ] A non-reserved `operationId` like `deleteItem` is unchanged
- [ ] An `operationId` that becomes a reserved word after sanitization (e.g. `delete!!`) is also suffixed
- [ ] Existing operationId sanitization (camelCase, digit prefix) still works correctly

## Tasks

- Added `RESERVED_WORDS` set covering all JS/TS reserved and future-reserved words to `operation-type-coder.js`
- Updated `sanitizeIdentifier` to append `_` when the result is a reserved word
- Added unit tests for direct reserved words, post-sanitization collisions, and non-colliding identifiers

detailed_source_records.title: Fix TypeError when response content has no schema
detailed_source_records.author: Copilot
detailed_source_records.body:
## Summary

When a response content entry defines only `examples` (no `schema`), the TypeScript type generator crashes with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'data')` and emits a useless error-comment stub type instead of a valid type.

**Root cause:** `SchemaTypeCoder` was constructed unconditionally with `content.get("schema")`, which returns `undefined` when the key is absent. The coder then blows up accessing `.data` on `undefined`.

**Fix:** Guard with `content.has("schema")` before constructing `SchemaTypeCoder`; fall back to `unknown` when absent.

```js
// Before — crashes when schema is missing
body?: ${new SchemaTypeCoder(content.get("schema")).write(script)}

// After — graceful fallback
body?: ${content.has("schema") ? new SchemaTypeCoder(content.get("schema")).write(script) : "unknown"}
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

When a response lacks a schema (e.g. only has `examples`), the generated type for that operation collapses to an empty `{}` containing only an error comment. This makes the `$` argument in the route handler lose all useful type information (request body, parameters, etc.). The requested behavior is to emit `unknown` for the response body type instead of crashing.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] `POST /stuff` with the issue's spec generates a valid `createStuff` type with `body?: unknown` for the 200 response — no error comment
- [x] The `$` argument in the generated route handler retains meaningful types for request body and parameters when response schema is absent
- [x] Response content that has both `examples` and a `schema` still generates the correctly typed body (no regression)
- [x] Response with no `content` at all still generates `{ status: N }` with no body field
- [x] OpenAPI 2 specs with schema-only responses are unaffected

## Tasks

- Guard `content.has("schema")` before constructing `SchemaTypeCoder` in `operation-type-coder.js` (`responseTypes`)
- Same guard in `response-type-coder.js` (`buildContentObjectType`)
- Unit tests covering the no-schema case in both coders
